definitions.explanation: A system of government in which a single ruler or small group holds absolute power without constitutional or democratic constraints. Used in historical, political, and academic contexts.

examples.japanese: {専制政治|せんせいせいじ}は{国民|こくみん}の{自由|じゆう}を{奪|うば}う。
examples.english: Autocratic rule robs the people of their freedom.

examples.japanese: フランス{革命|かくめい}は{専制政治|せんせいせいじ}に{対|たい}する{民衆|みんしゅう}の{反乱|はんらん}だった。
examples.english: The French Revolution was a popular uprising against despotic rule.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}にはいまだに{専制政治|せんせいせいじ}が{続|つづ}く{国|くに}があり、{国際社会|こくさいしゃかい}から{批判|ひはん}を{受|う}けている。
examples.english: There are still countries where autocratic rule continues, drawing criticism from the international community.

notes:
Composed of {専制|せんせい} (autocracy, despotism) and {政治|せいじ} (politics, government). The {専制|せんせい} component means exclusive or monopolistic control. A standard term in history textbooks and political science.

USAGE:
Commonly encountered in world history education when discussing absolute monarchies, dictatorships, and pre-modern political systems. Also used in contemporary commentary about authoritarian regimes. More formal and academic than simply calling a government {独裁|どくさい} (dictatorship).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {専制政治|せんせいせいじ}を{行|おこな}う: to carry out autocratic rule
- {専制政治|せんせいせいじ}を{打倒|だとう}する: to overthrow despotic rule
- {専制政治|せんせいせいじ}の{時代|じだい}: the era of autocratic rule
- {専制政治|せんせいせいじ}に{苦|くる}しむ: to suffer under despotism

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {独裁政治|どくさいせいじ}: dictatorship — emphasizes rule by a single dictator; more modern and direct
- {専制|せんせい}: autocracy, despotism — the shorter form, usable on its own as a noun
- {絶対王政|ぜったいおうせい}: absolute monarchy — specifically refers to monarchical despotism, as in pre-revolutionary France
- {民主政治|みんしゅせいじ}: democratic government — the opposite concept
